At least 7.5 EC of profiling must be outside the Veterinary faculty.

core: Comparative organismal, cellular, molecular and physiological foundations relevant to animal bodies and health
Infection, immunity, pathology, pharmacological mechanisms and disease processes across animals and populations
Epidemiological, laboratory, statistical and evidence-synthesis methods for animal-health research
adjacent: One Health links among animal health, human health, ecosystems, zoonoses, welfare, ethics and food systems

trace: develops programming and reproducible computational problem-solving for biological and epidemiological data
develops data cleaning, visualisation and project-based analysis for health, ecological and population observations
provides calculus and differential-equation foundations for quantitative biological and disease processes
develops probability, estimation and simulation for uncertain biological and epidemiological evidence
establishes cells, macromolecules, genetics, signalling and physiology as general life-science mechanisms while not claiming animal-specific anatomy
introduces neural and behavioural science plus experimental methods needed for later comparative neurobiology and evidence synthesis
studies eukaryotic and prokaryotic cell structure, physiology, genomes and molecular research methods that underlie organismal health
studies human homeostasis and organ-system physiology as transferable mammalian mechanisms, explicitly not as veterinary physiology
studies biomolecule chemistry, metabolism and molecular dysfunction across living organisms
practises blood, bacterial, protein, DNA and bioinformatic laboratory methods relevant to infection and biological investigation
studies inflammation, immunity, tissue repair, neoplasia and molecular genetics in human disease as related mechanisms rather than veterinary pathology
studies epidemiology, population health, disease risk and evaluation of interventions, directly supporting zoonotic and One Health reasoning
studies drug targets, pharmacokinetics, toxicity and dose-response as general pharmacological mechanisms while retaining the veterinary-pharmacology gap
directly studies host-pathogen interactions and immune responses affecting humans, animals and plants
derives pathophysiology from anatomy and physiology across human organ systems as related disease science, not animal diagnosis
directly compares animal neurobiology and anatomy, animal models, behaviour, laboratory methods and animal-welfare ethics
develops experimental design, regression and multivariate analysis for complex health and behavioural evidence
uses systematic review and meta-analysis to synthesise treatment and health evidence across studies
surveys animal, microbial and other biodiversity, including disease-causing organisms and methods for investigating living systems
studies biodiversity loss, conservation interventions and policy affecting animal populations and habitats
studies evolution from genes to populations as a foundation for species differences, adaptation and disease emergence
studies organism, population, community and ecosystem interactions, including animal biology, physiology and ecological modelling
examines marine organisms, ecological systems and human pressures as a concrete advanced animal-environment domain
examines sustainable livestock farming, food production and environmental impacts relevant to animal welfare and One Health
studies collective decision-making and policy for food, freshwater and climate sustainability as environmental-health governance
studies climate effects on ecosystems, food production and health as linked pressures on human and animal systems
develops ethical analysis through practical topics including animal rights, welfare-relevant responsibility and climate change

alternatives.label: Comparative biology, animal health & disease science
alternatives.concept: Study biological mechanisms relevant to animal health through cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, infection and immunity, pharmacology, disease mechanisms, comparative neurobiology, evolution and epidemiological research. Human-focused biomedical courses are used only for transferable mechanisms and are not presented as veterinary anatomy, diagnosis or clinical care.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines comparative and general life science, human biomedical mechanisms, infection, animal-relevant neurobiology, ecology and quantitative research; the label states related animal-health science without claiming veterinary medicine.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in Year 1 and seven level-300 courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term. Life-science foundations precede cell biology, physiology, biochemistry, laboratory work and advanced biomedical study; the brain-and-behaviour gateway precedes the research seminar; Mathematical Methods precedes Probability & Statistics.

alternatives.label: One Health, disease ecology & animal welfare
alternatives.concept: Connect infection and immunity, epidemiology, animal-relevant neurobiology and molecular disease science with biodiversity, evolution, ecosystems, conservation, sustainable livestock farming, climate pressures, ethics and environmental governance. This route studies human-animal-environment health relationships without claiming veterinary clinical training.
alternatives.labelReason: Four biomedical/mathematical courses are replaced by conservation, marine ecology, climate and sustainability-governance study, producing a clear One Health and welfare emphasis while retaining infection, disease and research foundations.
progression: The schedule contains 24 unique courses / 180 EC, four courses per semester, PPD in Year 1 and eight level-300 courses. Every formal prerequisite occurs earlier and every course is available in its assigned Fall-2026-start term. Life-science and brain-and-behaviour foundations precede laboratory, advanced disease, infection, neurobiology and research work; introductory biodiversity, evolution and ecosystem study support the advanced conservation, marine, farming and governance direction.
alternatives.distinctness: Four courses / 30 EC differ in each direction. Mathematical Methods, Molecular Cell Biology, Pharmacology and Probability & Statistics are replaced by Conservation Biology, Marine Biology, Climate Change and Governance of Sustainability. The change shifts curricular priority from biomedical mechanisms and quantitative disease science to ecosystem pressures, conservation and governance within One Health; it is not a cosmetic threshold substitution.

candidates.label: One Health, disease ecology and animal welfare
Veterinary diagnosis and clinical animal care

selection.assessment: Two complete related-field programmes pass the evidence, course-content, schedule and 30-EC distinctness gates. A third clinical veterinary route is not defensible because the workbook lacks veterinary anatomy and physiology, species-specific pathology, clinical examination and diagnostic training, animal nutrition and reproduction sequences, anaesthesia, surgery, clinical placements and veterinary capstone work. Human biomedical courses are not relabelled as those missing veterinary components.

notes.text: The UCR alternatives combine comparative and general biology, human biomedical mechanisms, infection and immunity, epidemiology, animal-relevant neurobiology, ecology, welfare ethics and One Health. They do not reproduce veterinary anatomy, species-specific pathology, clinical examination, diagnostics, animal nutrition and reproduction, anaesthesia, surgery, clinical skills or veterinary placements, and therefore represent related scientific routes rather than a Veterinary Medicine curriculum.
